title: No Filter: China's Rainbow Mountains Are 24M-Year-Old Rock | China Travel Expert
description:
No, China's Rainbow Mountains aren't Photoshopped. The stripes are 24 million years of real rock.

This is Zhangye Danxia (Qicai Danxia) in Gansu. The colors come from minerals in the sandstone — iron oxides for the reds and golds, other minerals for the greens — not paint or a filter. The layers were laid down in the Cretaceous, then tilted and buckled when the Indian and Eurasian plates collided, and erosion exposed the bands you see today. UNESCO listed it as part of China Danxia in 2010 and made it a Global Geopark in 2020.

🧭 Expert Tip: Come in the late afternoon on a dry day — low, warm sun saturates the stripes, and overcast light washes them flat. Tickets run about ¥100 incl. the shuttle in 2026 (check the official site zydanxia.cn; a ticket is often valid 2 days).
